title: Failover orchestrator: state machine + transition audit log; manual override endpoints w/ RBAC
author: Ethan Park
body:
Summary: Implements the core failover orchestrator state machine (authoritative source of truth for regional failover mode) and a structured audit log for all state transitions. Adds manual override endpoints (enable/disable/freeze/unfreeze, set target region, set progressive % stage) gated by RBAC and requiring a reason string. Motivation: For the regional failover automation upgrade, we need (1) an explicit state model that can be reasoned about and tested, (2) an auditable trail of who/what changed failover state and why, and (3) a safe manual escape hatch for on-call and controlled test windows.

State machine: The orchestrator owns a single FailoverPolicyState per (service_route, model, customer_tier_scope) tuple (initially scoped to hosted default routes only; dedicated/private will follow). States: HEALTHY -> DEGRADED (no traffic move; enables graceful-degradation knobs) -> FAILOVER_CANDIDATE (trigger engine recommends move; orchestrator runs safe-to-failover checks) -> FAILING_OVER (progressive routing steps) -> FAILED_OVER (steady-state) -> RECOVERING (progressive rollback) -> HEALTHY. Additional terminal-like/override states: FROZEN (no automatic transitions; manual only) and DISABLED (automation disabled; monitor-only). Transitions are idempotent and guarded with CAS semantics on state_version.

Audit log: Adds a FailoverTransitionAudit event for every transition attempt (including rejected/blocked transitions). Captures: actor_type (trigger_engine|human|system), actor_id (service identity or user email), authz_principal, request_id, correlation_id, from_state, to_state, decision (applied|no-op|rejected), rejection_reason, reason (human-supplied), trigger_snapshot (signal summary + computed scores), safety_checks_snapshot (capacity/dependency/policy sanity results), and timing (evaluated_at, applied_at). Audit records are written before and after apply to support debugging partial failures.

Manual override endpoints (control plane): POST /admin/failover/override/apply { scope, desired_state, target_region?, progressive_percent?, reason } and POST /admin/failover/override/freeze { scope, reason } /unfreeze. All manual endpoints require a reason and are gated behind RBAC: failover.admin (full), failover.operator (apply within allowed scopes; cannot change target_region), failover.viewer (read-only). RBAC checks use the standard Authorizer middleware and are wired to INT-881 group mappings (sre-oncall, release-eng, infra-netops). Overrides are also feature-flagged: failover_orchestrator_admin_endpoints (off by default in prod).

Operational behavior notes: (1) The orchestrator never directly mutates DNS/edge; it emits a routing-policy update request to the routing policy store (existing mechanism), then waits for confirmation/observability signals before advancing stages. (2) Progressive failover is modeled as a stage within FAILING_OVER/RECOVERING with stage_percent in state. (3) Any transition that would increase blast radius requires safe-to-failover checks to be green unless a user with failover.admin sets force=true (force is blocked in prod unless in an approved change window flag; see Connor’s notes below).

Testing: Adds unit tests for transition guards, idempotency, and audit record formation; integration tests for RBAC enforcement and state_version CAS collisions; basic "happy path" e2e using in-memory policy store in CI.

Rollout: No runtime behavior change for prod until the orchestrator is enabled via feature flag and trigger engine is configured to call it. This PR is a prerequisite for ENG-2848 (incident bot can link to audit trail) and upcoming safe-to-failover checks wiring.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): Persist audit log to long-retention store (currently 30d in control-plane DB), add UI surfacing in Console, and add metric counters for rejected/blocked transitions (Aisha filed a note; I added minimal metrics but not the full taxonomy).
commits: control-plane/failover: introduce state types + transition engine
control-plane/failover: add audit log model + writer
api: add admin override endpoints + request validation
authz: wire failover RBAC permissions + group mapping hooks
tests: state machine unit tests + RBAC integration tests
docs: internal API notes + runbook link placeholders
notable_snippets: Audit record (simplified): { from_state, to_state, decision, actor_type, actor_id, reason, trigger_snapshot, safety_checks_snapshot, request_id, correlation_id }
RBAC: requirePermission(req, 'failover.operator') for apply; requirePermission(req, 'failover.admin') for force or target_region changes
review_conversation: Mina Haddad: State machine looks good, but we need strict idempotency on repeated override/apply calls (operators will click twice). Can we treat same desired_state+scope+target_region as no-op and still write an audit record?

Ethan Park (author): Added idempotency: if desired matches current (including stage_percent/target_region) we emit decision=no-op audit entry and return 200 with current state_version. Added tests for duplicate submissions.
Zachary Hill: RBAC: please use Authorizer middleware, not the old group-check util. Also ensure service-to-service calls identify actor_id distinctly (not 'system').

Ethan Park (author): Swapped to Authorizer + permissions.ts registration. For mTLS service calls, actor_type=trigger_engine and actor_id=spiffe://redwood/trigger-engine; for humans, actor_id=email from SSO.

Connor O'Brien: Concern about "force" in prod. We should not allow force=true unless a release change window flag is enabled and request includes change_ticket_id. Otherwise this becomes an easy footgun during incidents.

Ethan Park (author): Implemented additional prod guard: force requires (1) failover.admin, (2) feature flag failover_orchestrator_force_override_prod enabled, and (3) change_ticket_id present. Logged into audit record. Added a failing test for missing ticket id.
Aisha Bello: Can we add a metric for rejected transitions and tag by rejection_reason? This will help detect flappy triggers / misconfigured thresholds.
Ethan Park (author): Added failover.transition_total{decision=applied|rejected|no-op} + failover.transition_rejection_total{reason=*}. Full taxonomy (per-signal) deferred to ENG-2847 dashboards work.

Miles Thornton: One nit: the transition guard currently allows HEALTHY -> FAILED_OVER via manual apply. I’d prefer that manual apply still goes through FAILING_OVER with progressive_percent defaulted to 10 and requires an explicit 'jump_to_100=true' for immediate cutover.
Ethan Park (author): Agreed. Updated manual apply behavior: defaults to FAILING_OVER stage=10 unless jump_to_100=true (admin only). Recorded in audit record (requested_behavior vs applied_behavior).
Miles Thornton: Approved after latest push. This unblocks wiring the trigger engine into orchestrator.
release_notes: Internal: Adds failover orchestrator state machine, audit log for state transitions, and RBAC-gated manual override endpoints (feature-flagged; no prod behavior change until enabled).
